Question Choices: A line that divides a figure into two matching reflected halves is called what?
Question Answers: line of symmetry|axis of symmetry|a line of symmetry
Hints: Folding along this line makes the halves coincide.|It is also called a reflection axis.
Solution: It is a line of symmetry, also called an axis of symmetry. Reflection across this line maps every point of the figure onto a point of the same figure.

Question Choices: How many lines of symmetry does a nonsquare rectangle have?
Hints: Consider the vertical and horizontal midlines.|Diagonal folds do not match here.
Solution: A nonsquare rectangle has two reflection axes: the lines through the center parallel to its sides. A diagonal would exchange unequal adjacent side lengths, so diagonals are not symmetry lines.

Question Choices: How many lines of symmetry does an equilateral triangle have?
Hints: Each fold passes through a vertex and the opposite midpoint.|There is one per vertex.
Solution: Each of the three lines from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side reflects an equilateral triangle onto itself. There are three lines of symmetry.

Question Choices: What is the smallest positive rotation that maps a square onto itself about its center?
Hints: A square has rotational symmetry of order 4.|Divide 360 by 4.
Solution: The regular polygon has 4 equally spaced vertices. The smallest matching turn advances one vertex position, so its angle is 360/4 = 90 degrees.

Question Choices: What is the smallest positive rotation that maps an equilateral triangle onto itself about its center?
Hints: Its rotational symmetry has order 3.|Divide 360 by 3.
Solution: The regular polygon has 3 equally spaced vertices. The smallest matching turn advances one vertex position, so its angle is 360/3 = 120 degrees.
